_comment: Release gates, grouped by guardrail layer. Thresholds are product decisions, set before looking at results and changed only in review, with the reason recorded. They are the release decision: tune the operating point (the score threshold in config/service.json) instead, never a gate. A gate with no value (n/a) fails. Spec 06 adds the remaining information gates and the ranking gates.

protectedFieldViolations.why: Authoritative fields (title, provider, RTP, stakes, max win, layout, jackpot network, status, brands, markets, season) must equal the rules-only normalisation: the model never writes them (AGENTS.md rule 3).

regulatedFieldsInvented.why: An RTP, stake or max win filled where the source had none would be a made-up regulated figure.

crypticRecordFabrications.why: An opaque record (an internal code and an unknown studio) carries no evidence, so any inferred matching field is a fabrication.

eligibilityViolations.why: A game that isn't live, is a test build, isn't on the brand, isn't licensed in the market, is out of season or has a restricted feature must never be shown. Checked against ground truth, so normalisation bugs count too.

duplicateViolations.why: Showing the seed's own game, or the same game twice (duplicate export or RTP variant), is a broken rail.

policyViolations.why: No rail may step a player up more than one volatility level, to more than 5x the seed's max bet or 10x its minimum bet (safer-gambling policy owned with compliance).

expectedDeclineRate.why: Title-only and opaque seeds carry no reliable evidence; recommending from them would be guessing.

coverage.why: Declining is right only when no good rail exists. Among queries the oracle can answer, at least 80% must be answered (false abstention at most 20%).
